source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Erect perennial herb to approx. 1.2 m, monoecious or dioecious; non-stinging (genus)
morphology_documented.leaves: Long-petioled ovate/ovate-lanceolate blades to 15 × 8 cm, serrate, 3 veins from base
morphology_documented.flowers: Dense tiny flower clusters along spike-like unbranched lateral inflorescences
morphology_documented.fruit: Ovate rounded winged one-seeded achene 1–1.5 mm, short beak
morphology_documented.habitat: Wet places and low streamside woods

source_scope_note: Direct species-level details separated from genus/key information; absent historical treatments not filled by unsupported inference.

Distinguish from stinging Urtica by absence of stinging hairs
preservation: Additive record only; photos, credits, species records and published site unchanged
